taxonomy:
Here's a taxonomy of grid-based logic games based on the provided rules:

**I. Placement/Coloring Games**

*   **Lighting/Illumination:**
    *   **Akari:** Place light bulbs in white squares; bulbs illuminate adjacent white squares (not other bulbs or black squares/frames). Numbered squares indicate adjacent bulbs.
*   **Area/Region Filling:**
    *   **Chained Block:** Fill cells with black and white. Black cells form "blocks" of specified sizes. Blocks touching at corners form "chains." Chains cannot have more than one block of a given size/shape.
    *   **Dotchi-Loop:** Paint some cells black. Black cells must form rectangles/squares. White cells must not form rectangles/squares. Numbers indicate the size of the area containing the cell.
    *   **Evolomino:** Divide grid into blocks. Each block contains a pair of areas (white/gray) with the same shape. Numbers indicate half the cells in a block.
    *   **Five Cells:** Draw squares in white cells. Connected squares form "blocks." Each block must contain exactly one square on an arrow. Arrows must pass through at least two blocks. Later blocks on an arrow's path must grow by one square.
    *   **Fillomino:** Divide grid into blocks of five cells. Numbers in cells indicate surrounding lines (including frame). Lines surround cells but don't enter blocks.
    *   **Heyawake:** Fill cells within rooms (bordered by bold lines). Rooms with numbers indicate the count of painted cells. White cells cannot span more than two rooms straight. Painted cells cannot connect horizontally/vertically; white cells cannot be separated by painted cells.
    *   **Hitori:** Color cells. No number appears more than once in a row or column. Sides of black cells never touch. White cells form a continuous network.
    *   **Kurodoko:** Color cells black. Numbers indicate white cells to the nearest black cell or frame. Cells with numbers remain white. Black cells don't touch; white cells must be connected.
    *   **Kurotto:** Color cells. Numbers in circles are the sum of continuous black cells extending vertically/horizontally. Cells with circles cannot be colored.
    *   **LITS:** Color four consecutive squares (tetrominoes) within areas. Similarly shaped tetrominoes can't touch (except at corners). Colored squares form a connected network. Colored squares cannot form 2x2 or larger.
    *   **Norinori:** Shade cells. Each outlined region has two blocks of the same number of shaded cells. Numbers indicate block size. All shaded cells are connected. Two blocks in a region don't touch. No 2x2 group can be entirely shaded.
    *   **Nurimeizu:** Paint cells to create a maze from S to G over white cells. Rooms (bordered by bold lines) must be entirely painted or white. White cells cannot be cut off or form a loop. S, G, circle, and triangle rooms are exceptions. Black and white cells cannot form 2x2 or larger.
    *   **Nurimisaki:** Fill cells. Circled cells remain white ("Misaki"). White Misaki cells have only one adjacent white cell. Numbers in circles indicate adjacent white cells in a straight line. White cells form a continuous network. Black/white cells cannot form 2x2 or larger.
    *   **Shakashaka:** Place black "triangles" in squares. Triangles are not placed in black squares. White areas form rectangles/squares. Numbers indicate adjacent black triangles.
    *   **Sto-stone:** Fill colored cells. Rooms (bordered by bold lines) indicate the number of continuous black cells. Rooms without numbers have any number of black cells. Black cells cannot cross room boundaries. When "dropped," stones fill the bottom half without empty cells.
    *   **Tilepaint:** Color tiles (bordered by bold lines). Numbers in cells with diagonal lines indicate black cells to the right/down in that line/column. Cells in a tile must be all colored or uncolored. Solution shows an object outline.
    *   **Usowan:** Fill colored cells. Cells with numbers cannot be colored. Numbers indicate adjacent colored cells (vertically/horizontally). Rooms have one wrong number. Colored cells cannot connect; white cells cannot be separated.

*   **Number/Value Placement:**
    *   **Choco Banana:** Fill cells with black/white. Black cells form "blocks" of specified sizes. Blocks touching at corners form "chains." Chains cannot have more than one block of a given size/shape.
    *   **Double Choco:** Divide grid into blocks. Blocks contain pairs of white/gray areas with the same shape. Numbers indicate cells of that color, equaling half the block's cells.
    *   **Makaro:** Fill cells. Numbers in circles indicate white cells forming a straight line from the Misaki cell. White cells form a continuous network. Black/white cells cannot form 2x2 or larger.
    *   **Nurikabe:** Fill cells. Numbers indicate continuous white cells. Areas of white cells have one number and are separated by black cells. Black cells form a continuous wall. Black cells cannot form 2x2 or larger.
    *   **Sudoku:** Place numbers 1-9 in each empty cell. Each row, column, and 3x3 block contains all numbers 1-9.

**II. Path/Loop Drawing Games**

*   **Loop Drawing (single path):**
    *   **Dotchi-Loop:** Draw lines through cell centers to make a single loop. Loop goes through white circles, not black. Loop can go straight or turn at white circles.
    *   **Masyu:** Draw a single loop through cell centers. Loop goes through all black/white circles. White circles: loop passes straight, turns at adjacent. Black circles: loop turns at the circle, then goes straight through the next cell.
    *   **Nagareru:** Draw a line to make a single continuous loop. Loop goes through cells with arrows (black), following arrow direction. Arrows show wind; loop cannot go against wind. Side winds necessitate movement in the wind's direction.
    *   **Suraromu:** Make a single loop through cell centers. Loop never crosses itself. Dotted lines between black cells/frame are "Gates." Loop must pass all Gates once. Loop starts and ends at an open numbered circle. Numbers on Gates show when they are crossed.
    *   **Yajilin:** Draw a single loop. Loop passes through cell centers. Numbers show black cells in arrow direction. Loop avoids black cells and numbered cells. Black cells cannot touch horizontally/vertically.

*   **Path/Line Drawing (connecting points):**
    *   **Hashiwokakero:** Connect islands (circles with numbers) with bridges, up to the number shown. Max two bridges between islands. Bridges don't cross islands/other bridges. Bridges form a continuous link.
    *   **Hebi:** Place numbers 1-5 in squares to represent snakes (head to tail). Snakes cannot touch sides. Viewed from 2→1, another snake part cannot be in the next black square or grid rim. Black squares show the nearest number in the arrow's direction (0 means no snake).
    *   **Numberlink:** Connect pairs of same numbers with a continuous line. Lines go through cell centers, don't cross, branch off, or go through numbered cells.
    *   **Pencils:** Draw lines from pencil tips. Lines go through cells. Numbers show pencil length. Lines cannot cross or branch off.
    *   **Slitherlink:** Connect adjacent dots with vertical/horizontal lines to make a single loop. Numbers indicate surrounding lines. Empty cells have any surrounding line count. Loop doesn't cross itself or branch.

*   **Path/Line Drawing (specific movement rules):**
    *   **Mid-loop:** Draw lines to make a single loop. Loop through cell centers, never crossing. Loop through all black circles, using them as midpoints.
    *   **Moon-or-Sun:** Draw a single loop. Loop through cell centers. Rooms (bordered by bold lines) are entered only once. In each room, loop goes through all moon OR all sun cells. After moons in one room, must go through suns in the next room, and vice versa.
    *   **Yosenabe:** Move circles vertically/horizontally into gray areas. Arrows show movement. Arrows don't bend, cross others, or go through lines. Gray area numbers equal the sum of circles entering. Empty gray areas have any sum, but at least one circle must enter.

**III. Block/Shape Division Games**

*   **Block/Region Formation:**
    *   **Fillomino:** Divide grid into blocks of five cells. Numbers in cells indicate surrounding lines (including frame). Lines surround cells but don't enter blocks.
    *   **Sashigane:** Divide grid into L-shaped blocks, one block wide. Blocks must be L-shaped. Open circles form the knee. Numbers in open circles show block cell count. Arrows indicate block end. Marks (arrows/circles) can be 0, 1, 2, or 3.

**IV. Grid Transformation/Movement Games**

*   **Movements/Transformations:**
    *   **Choco Banana:** Fill cells with black/white. Black cells form "blocks" of specified sizes. Blocks touching at corners form "chains." Chains cannot have more than one block of a given size/shape.
    *   **Double Choco:** Divide grid into blocks. Blocks contain pairs of white/gray areas with the same shape. Numbers indicate cells of that color, equaling half the block's cells.
    *   **Satogaeri:** Move circles (vertically/horizontally) so each country (bordered by bold lines) has one circle. Numbers in circles indicate cells to pass through. Circles without numbers move any distance. Circles cannot cross other circles' tracks or go over them.

**V. Number/Value Relation Games**

*   **Constraint-Based Number Placement:**
    *   **Chained Block:** Fill cells with black/white. Black cells form "blocks" of specified sizes. Blocks touching at corners form "chains." Chains cannot have more than one block of a given size/shape.
    *   **Choco Banana:** Fill cells with black/white. Black cells form "blocks" of specified sizes. Blocks touching at corners form "chains." Chains cannot have more than one block of a given size/shape.
    *   **Evolomino:** Divide grid into blocks. Each block contains a pair of areas (white/gray) with the same shape. Numbers indicate half the cells in a block.
    *   **Fillomino:** Divide grid into blocks of five cells. Numbers in cells indicate surrounding lines (including frame). Lines surround cells but don't enter blocks.
    *   **Heyawake:** Fill cells within rooms (bordered by bold lines). Rooms with numbers indicate the count of painted cells. White cells cannot span more than two rooms straight. Painted cells cannot connect horizontally/vertically; white cells cannot be separated by painted cells.
    *   **Kurodoko:** Color cells black. Numbers indicate white cells to the nearest black cell or frame. Cells with numbers remain white. Black cells don't touch; white cells must be connected.
    *   **Nurikabe:** Fill cells. Numbers indicate continuous white cells. Areas of white cells have one number and are separated by black cells. Black cells form a continuous wall. Black cells cannot form 2x2 or larger.
    *   **Nuritwin:** Shade cells. Each outlined region has two blocks of the same number of shaded cells. Numbers indicate block size. All shaded cells are connected. Two blocks in a region don't touch. No 2x2 group can be entirely shaded.
    *   **Ripple Effect:** Rooms (bordered by bold lines) contain consecutive numbers from 1. Duplicated numbers in a row/column have a space between them equal to or greater than the number's value.
    *   **Shikaku:** Numbers indicate adjacent black triangles (vertically/horizontally).
    *   **Slitherlink:** Connect adjacent dots with vertical/horizontal lines to make a single loop. Numbers indicate surrounding lines. Empty cells have any surrounding line count. Loop doesn't cross itself or branch.
    *   **Sto-stone:** Fill colored cells. Rooms (bordered by bold lines) indicate the number of continuous black cells. Rooms without numbers have any number of black cells. Black cells cannot cross room boundaries. When "dropped," stones fill the bottom half without empty cells.
    *   **Sudoku:** Place numbers 1-9 in each empty cell. Each row, column, and 3x3 block contains all numbers 1-9.
    *   **Yajilin:** Numbers show black cells in arrow direction. Loop avoids black cells and numbered cells.

**VI. Uncategorized (Based on provided rules, insufficient for placement):**

*   **Nansuke:** Fill blank cells with numbers from a list. Numbers are up-down or left-to-right.
*   **Akari:** Place light bulbs in white squares; bulbs illuminate adjacent white squares (not other bulbs or black squares/frames). Numbered squares indicate adjacent bulbs.
*   **Hebi:** Place numbers 1-5 in squares to represent snakes (head to tail). Snakes cannot touch sides. Viewed from 2→1, another snake part cannot be in the next black square or grid rim. Black squares show the nearest number in the arrow's direction (0 means no snake).
*   **Juosan:** Fill cells with "-" or "|". Areas (Territories) show how many marks they get. Territories without numbers have any number of marks. Marks extend horizontally (max 3 cells), vertically (max 2 cells).
*   **Nurimisaki:** Fill cells. Circled cells remain white ("Misaki"). White Misaki cells have only one adjacent white cell. Numbers in circles indicate adjacent white cells in a straight line. White cells form a continuous network. Black/white cells cannot form 2x2 or larger.
*   **Numberlink:** Connect pairs of same numbers with a continuous line. Lines go through cell centers, don't cross, branch off, or go through numbered cells.
